graph_meta.description: Simplify m⁵n¹² ÷ (mn)⁹ using the quotient rule and power of a product rule.

nodes.label: Identify Variables and Powers
nodes.description: Identify the variables and exponents in the expression.
hints: Notice the numerator has m and n, and the denominator is a power of mn.

nodes.label: Identify the Goal
nodes.prompt: What do we need to do?
hints: Use exponent laws to simplify the quotient.

nodes.label: Problem Statement
nodes.prompt: How would you begin simplifying m⁵n¹² ÷ (mn)⁹?
hints: The denominator has a product raised to a power. Think about expanding it first.
Use the Power of a Product Rule: (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ.
Expand (mn)⁹ = m⁹n⁹, then apply the Quotient Rule.

nodes.label: Method 1: Expand Denominator First
nodes.description: Expand (mn)⁹ = m⁹n⁹ using the Power of a Product Rule, then apply Quotient Rule.
accept: power of a product rule: m⁹n⁹
distribute the exponent 9 to m and n
m to the 9 times n to the 9
hints: Use the Power of a Product Rule: (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ.

nodes.label: Apply Quotient Rule to m
nodes.prompt: After expanding the denominator, simplify m⁵ ÷ m⁹ using the Quotient Rule.
hints: Subtract the exponents: m⁵ ÷ m⁹ = m^(5−9).

nodes.label: Apply Quotient Rule to n
hints: Apply the Quotient Rule to the n terms.

nodes.label: Combine and Write Final Form
nodes.prompt: Combine m⁻⁴ and n³ into a single simplified expression.
accept: n cubed divided by m to the 4
hints: You have m⁻⁴ × n³. Rewrite the negative exponent as a denominator.

nodes.label: Method 2: Quotient Rule Step-by-Step
nodes.description: Separately apply Quotient Rule to m and n terms using the structure of the division.
nodes.prompt: Without fully expanding (mn)⁹, how can you split the division into separate fractions for m and n?
accept: split into m part and n part
separate the m and n terms
quotient rule applied separately to m and n
hints: Handle m and n independently using the Quotient Rule.

nodes.label: Quotient Rule on m: m⁵/m⁹
nodes.prompt: Apply the Quotient Rule to the m terms: m⁵ ÷ m⁹.

nodes.label: Quotient Rule on n: n¹²/n⁹
nodes.prompt: Apply the Quotient Rule to the n terms: n¹² ÷ n⁹.

nodes.label: Combine: m⁻⁴ × n³
nodes.prompt: Write the combined result m⁻⁴ × n³ with positive exponents only.
accept: n cubed over m to the 4
hints: Express m⁻⁴ with a positive exponent by moving it to the denominator.

nodes.label: Final Answer
nodes.prompt: What is the fully simplified form of m⁵n¹² ÷ (mn)⁹?
accept: n cubed over m to the fourth
hints: Both methods should give the same expression.
The answer uses positive exponents only.
